hadiths.arabicText: عَنْ /94 مَعْمَرٍ ، عَنِ /26 الزُّهْرِيِّ ، عَنْ /26 سَالِمٍ ، /27 عَنِ /93 ابْنِ عُمَرَ أَنَّ رَجُلا قَالَ لِلَّنِبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : إِنِّي /20 رَأَيْتُ لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ
hadiths.english_translation: From Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: I saw Laylat al-Qadr (in a dream), as if it was such and such night. He said: I see that your dreams have agreed upon the last ten nights, so seek it in the last nine, in an odd night

hadiths.english_translation: From Ma'mar and Ibn Jurayj, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Seek Laylat al-Qadr in the last ten nights (al-ghawabir), in the last nine (al-ghawabir), in an odd night. Also: From Ma'mar and Ibn Jurayj that they both heard Ibn Shihab narrating from Urwah, from Aisha, and from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform i'tikaf in the last ten nights of Ramadan until Allah caused him to die

hadiths.arabicText: عَنْ /94 مَعْمَرٍ ، عَنْ /26 أَبِي هَارُونَ الْعَبْدِيِّ ، /27 عَنْ /93 أَبِي سَعِيدٍ   الْخُدْرِيِّ
hadiths.english_translation: From Ma'mar, from Abu Harun al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, he said: We performed i'tikaf with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the middle ten nights of Ramadan, and we left on the morning of the twentieth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us and said: I saw Laylat al-Qadr, then I was made to forget it, so seek it in the last ten nights, in an odd night. And I saw that I was prostrating in water and mud, so whoever performed i'tikaf with me, let him return to his place of i'tikaf. We returned and there was not a cloud in the sky, then a cloud came and we were rained upon until the roof of the mosque flowed, and it was made of palm fronds. Prayer was called and I saw on the tip of the nose of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he finished, traces of mud on his forehead and nose, meaning the night of the twenty-first. Also from al-Thawri, from Abu Harun, from Abu Sa'id, similarly, except that he said: He performed i'tikaf, and we performed i'tikaf with him

hadiths.arabicText: عَنْ /94 مَعْمَرٍ ، عَنْ /26 يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي كَثِيرٍ ، عَنْ /26 أَبِي سَلَمَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ ، قَالَ : /27 تَذَاكَرْنَا لَيْلَةَ الْقَدْرِ
hadiths.english_translation: From Ma'mar, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, he said: We discussed Laylat al-Qadr among a group from Quraysh, so I came to Abu Sa'id al-Khudri who was a friend of mine, and I said: Won't you come out with us to the palm groves? He said: Yes. He came out wearing his striped cloak. I said to him: Did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mention Laylat al-Qadr? He said: Yes, we performed i'tikaf with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the middle ten nights of Ramadan, and we left on the morning of the twentieth. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ addressed us and said: I saw Laylat al-Qadr, then I was made to forget it, so seek it in the last ten nights, in an odd night. And I saw that I was prostrating in water and mud, so whoever performed i'tikaf with me, let him return to his place of i'tikaf. We returned and there was not a speck of cloud in the sky, then a cloud came and we were rained upon until the roof of the mosque flowed - and it was made of palm fronds - and prayer was established. I saw on the tip of the nose of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he finished, traces of mud on his forehead and nose, meaning the night of the twenty-first. Also: From Ibn Jurayj, from Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid, he said: Ibn Abbas used to sprinkle water on his family on the night of the twenty-third

hadiths.arabicText: عَنِ /94 ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ ، قَالَ : أَخْبَرَنِي /26 يُونُسُ بْنُ سِيفٍ ، أَنَّهُ /27 سَمِعَ /26 ابْنَ الْمُسَيِّبِ
hadiths.english_translation: From Ibn Jurayj, he said: Yunus ibn Sayf informed me that he heard Ibn al-Musayyib say: The Prophet ﷺ was among a group of his Companions, and he said: Shall I not inform you about Laylat al-Qadr? They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah! He was silent for a while, then said: I had just said to you what I said a moment ago while I knew it, and I still know it, then I was made to forget it. Do you recall a day when we were in such and such place - in a battle he fought - which night was it? They said: We traveled and did such and such, until the group agreed that it was the night of the twenty-third

hadiths.english_translation: From Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, he said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah! I saw in a dream Laylat al-Qadr, as if it was the seventh night. The Prophet ﷺ said: I see that your dreams have agreed on the seventh night, so whoever wishes to seek it, let him seek it on the seventh night. Ma'mar said: Ayyub used to perform ghusl on the night of the twenty-third and apply perfume
plainChains: Ma'mar -> Ayyub -> Nafi' -> Ibn Umar -> Prophet ﷺ

potential_issues.issue: Multiple uses of 'an (عَنْ) throughout the chain
potential_issues.impact: However, all narrators are highly reliable (Thiqah Thabt) and this specific chain is one of the golden chains of hadith. None are known mudallisun.

hadiths.english_translation: From Ma'mar, from Ayyub and others, from some of them, that al-Juhani came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah! I am a man of the desert with livestock, so advise me about Laylat al-Qadr to worship in it. The Prophet ﷺ said: Or two nights? He said: Rather one night. So he called him and whispered to him - no one knows what he ordered him. The people said: Watch which night al-Juhani worships. So whenever it was the night of the twenty-third, he would come down to his family and worship that night
plainChains: Ma'mar -> Ayyub & others -> Unknown narrator(s) -> (al-Juhani Companion) -> Prophet ﷺ

potential_issues.impact: This creates a disconnection due to majhul (unknown) narrator. The chain cannot be verified.

hadiths.english_translation: From Ibn Jurayj, he said: I was informed that al-Juhani, Abdullah ibn Unays, came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah! I have a heavy burden and farmland - and he was a farmer - so command me a night. He said: Or two nights? He said: Rather one night. So he called him and whispered to him two or three times, and commanded him the night of the twenty-third. He used to spend that night in the mosque and would not leave it until he went out in the morning, and he would not witness any of Ramadan before or after it, nor the day of Eid

hadiths.arabicText: عَنْ /94 مَالِكٍ ، /27 عَنْ /26 أَبِي النَّضْرِ ، أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ أُنَيْسٍ الْجُهَنِيَّ

hadiths.english_translation: From al-Thawri, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, he said: I heard those who say: It is the night of the seventeenth, and those who say: It is the night of the twenty-first, and those who say: It is the night of the twenty-third, and those who say: It is the night of the twenty-seventh. So I said to Salamah: You are older than us and have longer companionship (with scholars), and they differ. He said: Do not say that, rather seek it in the last ten nights

hadiths.arabicText: عَنِ /94 ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ ، قَالَ : أَخْبَرَنِي /26 عَمْرُو بْنُ دِينَارٍ
hadiths.english_translation: From Ibn Jurayj, he said: Amr ibn Dinar informed me, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, the Prophet ﷺ said: I was shown Laylat al-Qadr, then I forgot it. And it is in the last ten nights, and it is an odd night. I saw myself prostrating in water and mud on its morning. It rained on us on the night of the twenty-third, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in prayer that morning, and I looked at him when he left - mud and water were on his forehead and nose
